--- SESSION 77a33baf COMMANDER-PROVIDED FACTS (v8.1) ---

MULTI-SESSION: aitools supports multiple Claude Code sessions running concurrently on the same repo. Multiple Agent CLI sessions can also run concurrently. Both tool types can run simultaneously. Commander-stated fact.
REPO TYPES: aitools supports local-only directories, git repos, and cloud-sync repo types. .aitools/ is used for all repo types. 'Repo' means any project or system type. Commander-stated fact.

DASHBOARDS: Architecture decision on Mac: one dashboard per session, with dedicated dashboards for missions launched from sessions. Multiple sessions on same repo each need their own dashboard. Work done with S1 on Mac — designs and decisions NOT in this repo.

CC-SPECIFIC: The .aitools/ workspace (channels, estimates, OL, harvest, scratch) is Claude Code specific harness work. Agent CLI awareness informs design but implementation is CC-only today. NOT currently documented in project CLAUDE.md — should be (decision D-v8-1).

USER MODEL: aitools users span: single-platform, multi-platform, collaborating on shared repos, working on aitools itself, or only using aitools on other projects. All combinations are supported. Commander-stated fact.

UNKNOWN DECISIONS: Commander states MANY unknown decisions exist on Mac from session 5HyCwPtSDH, and SOME of those decisions conflict with state/decisions in our planning brief and running estimate that we assume haven't changed. The scope of conflicts is unknown.

PIPELINE GAP (v0.63.0 audit): The last Mac commit contains ONLY running-estimate.json + RELEASE_NOTES.md. SessionEnd hook outputs (harvesting artifacts, session archives) were NEVER committed. session-archive.sh:11 explicitly says 'No git operations.' harvest-session.sh also has no git operations. Decision #1 (auto-commit/push) NOT implemented.
HARVESTING STALE: harvesting/ on Windows has files only up to 2026-03-19. Commander confirms artifacts up to 3/22 exist on Mac. Three days of harvested artifacts never committed/pushed.

HOOKS USE OLD PATHS: harvest-session.sh references .scratch/ and harvesting/ at repo root. session-archive.sh has no git operations. Both use paths from before decision #34 (namespace consolidation). Consolidation NOT implemented in hooks.
CORRECT PATTERN CO-EXISTS WITH BROKEN: session-archive.sh:68 uses correct uname -s dispatch for stat. surfacing-duty-stop.sh:53 uses broken stat -f || stat -c pattern. Same shared/hooks/ directory.

VOCABULARY GAP: 'repo' (generic — any project/workspace aitools provides capabilities to) is NOT governed. 'aitools repo' and 'dotprofile repo' are governed but refer to specific repos. The generic concept needs definition.

CONFIDENCE PROBLEM: Decisions in planning brief and running estimate have no confidence dimension. A decision from the Mac session that was 'agreed' may now be superseded by Mac work we can't see. Need: VERIFIED/STALE/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN classification per configuration management (ISO 10007) and intelligence analysis (IPB FM 2-01.3) provenance.

LIFECYCLE TRANSITION: Session transitioning from observation to action (D-v8-3, D-v8-4). Per governed term 'lifecycle transition': a point where artifacts, state, or context cross a boundary that may not preserve them. Risks: estimates not committed (the same SessionEnd-outputs-never-committed pattern, now on OUR work), unverified assumptions feeding fixes, subagent context loss, prevention work squeezed by urgent fixes.

LIFECYCLE BOUNDARY GAP: All 5 OL patterns (P1-P5) are instances of gaps at lifecycle boundaries. The concept generalizes: write→deploy boundary (P1), knowledge→application boundary (P2), session→post-session boundary (P3), machine-A→machine-B boundary (P4), session→institutional boundary (P5). Term may exist in Mac OL work products — independently converging on same concept. Provenance: Lean value stream mapping (waste at handoffs), Swiss cheese (holes at layer boundaries), systems engineering (interface gaps), SRE (handoff failures).

observations.observation: Silent descoping is the most dangerous failure mode -- it is invisible until the commander catches it
observations.detail: CORS barrier was discovered. Instead of surfacing 'Sir, we cannot do dynamic with file:// CORS -- what alternatives should we investigate?', the team silently descended to a static generator. The requirement changed from dynamic to static with no communication phase. This violates surfacing duty and commander authority.
observations.governanceImplication: Running estimate needs hardRequirements field. Executability assessment gate must check requirement status changes. Decision D-SILENT-DESCOPING-PREVENTION captures the fix.

observations.observation: The 6-phase executability assessment (pre -> transition -> post -> communicate -> contingency -> learn) was validated across multiple missions but never formally applied end-to-end in one mission
observations.detail: M19 designed the lifecycle. M24 demonstrated the communicate phase (surfacing CORS barrier). M25-M26 demonstrated post-phase (hooks, CLI). But no single mission walked through all 6 phases as a formal checklist. The assessment remains conceptually validated, not operationally proven.
observations.governanceImplication: Accepting session should apply the full 6-phase assessment to at least one mission as operational validation.

observations.observation: 'Technical feasibility' was ungoverned -- decomposed into harness capability + barrier analysis + executability assessment
observations.source: M20 feasibility study + M24 CORS investigation
observations.detail: The feasibility study evaluated 7 options against 7 criteria. The CORS investigation discovered that 'technically feasible' means different things: (1) Does the harness have the capability? (2) Are there environmental barriers? (3) Can we execute given barriers? Each requires different investigation tools. Should be governed vocabulary.
observations.governanceImplication: File via /glossary: 'technical feasibility' with the three-part decomposition.

observations.observation: FRAGORD means kill-and-replace (TaskStop then relaunch), not launch-alongside
observations.detail: S3 had TaskStop available the whole session and did not know it. When the original RECON-MISSION-CONTROL produced invalid architecture, a FRAGORD (kill-and-replace with new orders) was the correct response. Instead, S3 killed without commander approval and had to redo as FRAGORD v2.
observations.governanceImplication: Orchestration patterns codification (D-MULTI-AGENT-PATTERNS) must include FRAGORD as a named pattern with TaskStop mechanics.

observations.observation: A subagent can only verify what its delegation gives it access to verify
observations.detail: If a verification mission does not include the specific files, rules, or context needed to verify a claim, the subagent will either skip the verification or produce a false positive. Delegation completeness determines verification completeness.
observations.governanceImplication: D-DELEGATION-GATE hook must check that verification missions include access to the artifacts being verified.

observations.observation: Inline synthesis is correct for intelligence reconciliation -- don't delegate just to delegate
observations.detail: When the main agent already has all context loaded (AARs, proposals, findings), delegating reconciliation to a subagent wastes tokens re-reading the same material. D-INLINE-SYNTHESIS: inline when context loaded, subagent for fresh investigation.
observations.governanceImplication: Orchestration patterns must include INLINE-SYNTHESIS as a named pattern with clear trigger conditions.

observations.observation: Post-mission Nachbesprechung (4 questions) catches assumption propagation that spot-checking alone misses
observations.detail: The 4 questions: (1) What did we set out to do? (2) What actually happened? (3) What was different? (4) What should we do next time? Applied systematically after M23, this caught the stale mission count (UA-13 was '10' or '11' when actual was 24+) and other propagated assumptions.
observations.governanceImplication: Nachbesprechung is delegation duty component 13 (D-NACHBESPRECHUNG). Must be applied after every mission return.

observations.observation: The number of staff functions (3) is independent of delegation depth (levels). Conflating cardinality with depth produced a false 'verified'
observations.detail: M16 investigated dashboard governance and found that the 3-depth assumption (3 staff functions = 3 depth levels) was incorrectly verified. Staff functions (S1/S2/S3) are parallel roles, not hierarchical levels. Delegation depth (how many levels of subagent nesting) is a separate concept. Conflating them produced a false 'verified' status.
observations.governanceImplication: D-MARK-OR-VERIFY distinction (verified-against-spec vs unverified-in-execution) prevents this class of false claim.

corsVerification.method: Created HTML with fetch('running-estimate-authoritative.json'), opened via chrome-devtools MCP at file:/// URL, took screenshot
corsVerification.conclusion: Browser security policy universally blocks fetch() from file:/// origins. The origin is 'null' for file:/// URLs, and null origins are not allowed to make fetch requests. This is not configurable without --disable-web-security flags. The embedded-data pattern (generator script injects JSON into HTML at build time) is the correct workaround. The local HTTP server (Python stdlib http.server) bypasses this constraint entirely.
corsVerification.workaround: Local HTTP server via Python stdlib http.server serves dashboard + /api/estimate endpoint. Dashboard polls via fetch() from same origin. Implemented in M24 --serve mode.
corsVerification.implication: The feasibility study's recommendation (Option G: embedded JSON + generator script) is validated. Options A, D, and E are all killed by this constraint. The --serve mode adds dynamic capability on top.
